pr_title: Fix test timeout for health on master failover
pr_body:
testHealthOnMasterFailover could timeout on some of the health requests
in the case where an index is added, since the recovery leads to
extended test run time.

Relates #61709

Closes #62690

comments: More-or-less the same in 7.x in https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/ewpzoilzkswwo, just wrapped in a `RemoteTransportException`.

This just failed again on 7.x: https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/trfozwsnowjw6. I muted the test:
* 4fa1f83b2425caed5cc00a56494a8de59e2cbc9d (master)
* 7ba0c95191f34c09540b826dc294d9614760f2d9 (7.x)

This is still happening on master I'm afraid. E.g. https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/dpyugiitqgvpm/tests/:server:internalClusterTest/org.elasticsearch.cluster.ClusterHealthIT/testHealthOnMasterFailover#1 just now

Another one on 7.x: https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/fxdf2nhcc25fi

Same error:
> java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException: MasterNotDiscoveredException[NodeClosedException[node closed {node_s1}{HvyOjBSUQkCM_E8UaszeRg}{WCl2aAdjR-C_6cO87R06AA}{127.0.0.1}{127.0.0.1:39953}{imr}]]; nested: NodeClosedException[node closed {node_s1}{HvyOjBSUQkCM_E8UaszeRg}{WCl2aAdjR-C_6cO87R06AA}{127.0.0.1}{127.0.0.1:39953}{imr}];	

I was able to reproduce it locally the first time I tried: https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/47syfrfzwglp4
But then it always succeeded.

Following does not reproduce it locally, but formed the basis of the optimization in #64378 so thought I would record it here:

```
./gradlew ':server:internalClusterTest' --tests "org.elasticsearch.cluster.ClusterHealthIT.testHealthOnMasterFailover" -Dtests.seed=7ACE2E890E81A58A -Dtests.security.manager=true -Dtests.locale=es-HN -Dtests.timezone=America/Antigua -Druntime.java=11
```

Both failures above (Armin/Yang comments) seem to be when we run with WindowsFS and seem to be timeout related.

The new instance did not reproduce for me. Investigating [build-stats](https://build-stats.elastic.co/app/kibana#/discover?_g=(refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-90d,mode:quick,to:now))&_a=(columns:!(branch,build.job-name),index:b646ed00-7efc-11e8-bf69-63c8ef516157,interval:auto,query:(language:lucene,query:testHealthOnMasterFailover),sort:!(process.time-start,desc))) it looks like it only happens on darwin.  The 7.10 build failures can be ignored (the previous fix is not in 7.10, not sure why those builds ran). Will investigate further.

review_comments: Just for my understanding: We took more than 1 minute here to get 20 (empty) shards to recover? Isn't that indicative of some other issue?
That time could include the 10 master restarts as well as some recovery time. The health call may not be able to respond until the settings are updated below.
